focus: Weak 'if' /ɪf/ and 'll /l/ · pausing at the comma between clauses · weak 'when/as soon as/unless' · intonation across two clauses · linking 'if I' → /ɪfaɪ/
focus_ar: 'if' و 'll الخفيفة، والوقف عند الفاصلة بين الجملتين، و 'when/as soon as/unless' الخفيفة، ونغمة الجملتين
arabic_challenge: Conditionals have two clauses with a specific melody: the 'if' clause rises slightly and pauses, then the result clause falls. Arabic learners tend to stress 'if' and deliver both clauses flat, losing the conditional 'shape'.

isolation.instructions: 'If' is an unstressed function word: /ɪf/. 'If it rains' = /ɪf ɪt ˈreɪnz/. The stress goes on the content of the clause (rains), not on 'if'.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'if' كلمة وظيفية غير منبورة /ɪf/. النبر على محتوى الجملة (rains) مش على 'if'.

sentence_practice: If it rains, we'll stay home.
If you come, I'll be happy.
If I have time, I'll help.
daily_drills.record_this: If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay home. If you come to the party, I'll be really happy. And if I have time this weekend, I'll help you move.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'if it rains'. Does 'if' stay light, with the stress on 'rains'?

target_sounds: pausing at the comma between clauses

isolation.instructions: When the 'if' clause comes first, pause slightly at the comma: 'If it rains, // we'll stay home'. The pause separates condition from result and makes the sentence clear.
isolation.instructions_ar: لما جملة 'if' تيجي الأول، قف قليلًا عند الفاصلة: 'If it rains, // we'll stay home'.
practice: If it rains, // we'll STAY home
If you're late, // we'll GO without you

sentence_practice: If it rains, we'll stay home.
If you need help, just call me.
If we leave now, we'll catch the train.
daily_drills.record_this: If it rains, we'll stay home and watch a film. If you need any help, just call me. And if we leave now, we'll easily catch the early train.
daily_drills.self_check: Do you pause slightly at the comma, so the two clauses are clearly separate?

isolation.instructions: The 'if' clause rises slightly at the comma (unfinished ↗), then the result clause falls to a finish (↘): 'If you study, ↗ you'll pass ↘'. This melody signals a conditional.
isolation.instructions_ar: جملة 'if' ترتفع قليلًا عند الفاصلة ↗، وبعدين جملة النتيجة تهبط للنهاية ↘. اللحن ده بيدل على الشرط.
practice: If we hurry, ↗ we'll make it ↘

sentence_practice: If we hurry, we'll make it.
daily_drills.record_this: If you study hard, you'll pass the exam. If we hurry now, we'll make it on time. And if you practise every day, you'll definitely improve your English.
daily_drills.self_check: Does your voice rise gently at the comma and then fall to finish the result?

isolation.instructions: Future time clauses use present tense after weak connectors: 'when' /wən/, 'as soon as' /əz suːn əz/, 'unless' /ənˈles/. 'I'll call you when I arrive' — stress 'call' and 'arrive'.
isolation.instructions_ar: جُمَل الزمن المستقبلية بتستخدم المضارع بعد روابط خفيفة: when، as soon as، unless. النبر على الفعلين.

sentence_practice: I'll call you when I arrive.
I'll come as soon as I can.
Unless you hurry, you'll be late.
daily_drills.record_this: I'll call you when I arrive at the airport. I'll come and help as soon as I can. And unless you hurry up now, you'll definitely be late for the meeting.
daily_drills.self_check: Note: use the PRESENT after 'when/as soon as/unless', never 'will'. Did you?

isolation.instructions: Vowel-to-vowel linking: 'if I' → /ɪfaɪ/, 'if it' → /ɪfɪt/. And the result clause contracts: 'I'll', 'we'll'. The whole conditional flows: 'ɪfaɪ have time, aɪl help'.
isolation.instructions_ar: وصل حرف علة بحرف علة: 'if I' → /ɪfaɪ/. وجملة النتيجة تتقلّص: I'll. الشرط كله يسيل.

sentence_practice: If I have time, I'll call you.
If it works, we'll be happy.
If I were you, I'd wait.
daily_drills.record_this: If I have time this evening, I'll call you. If it works the first time, we'll be really happy. And honestly, if I were you, I'd wait a little longer before deciding.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'if I have time'. Do 'if I' link smoothly into /ɪfaɪ/?

challenge_sentences: If it rains, we'll stay home.
I'll call you as soon as I arrive.
Unless you hurry, you'll miss the bus.
If I have time, I'll help you when you're ready.
daily_drills.record_this: If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay home. I'll call you as soon as I arrive at the hotel. Unless you hurry now, you'll miss the bus. And if I have time this weekend, I'll help you when you're ready.
daily_drills.self_check: Three checks: weak 'if', a pause + rise-fall melody, and present tense after when/as soon as/unless.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself talking about real future possibilities. Then listen back and check each feature.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك وانت تتكلم عن احتمالات مستقبلية واقعية، وبعدين اسمع وراجع كل نقطة.
test_yourself.passage: I have a big exam next week, so I've made a plan. If I study hard every day, I'll be ready in time. If I don't understand something, I'll ask my teacher. I'll start early each morning, and I won't check my phone unless I finish my goals. As soon as the exam is over, I'm going to relax. If I pass, my family will be very proud, and we'll celebrate together. If I don't pass, I won't give up — I'll simply try again. Either way, if I do my best, I'll be happy with myself. When the results come out, I'll call you immediately.

sounds_to_check.weak 'if': if I study, if I don't understand, if I pass, if I do my best
sounds_to_check.comma pause + rise/fall: If I study hard, ↗ I'll be ready ↘
sounds_to_check.'ll in the result: I'll be ready, I'll ask, we'll celebrate, I'll try again, I'll call
sounds_to_check.when/as soon as/unless + present: as soon as the exam is over, unless I finish, when the results come out
sounds_to_check.linking 'if I': if I study, if I pass, if I do my best

scoring_guide.90_100: Weak 'if', clear two-clause melody, present after time words. Ready for week 5.
scoring_guide.70_89: Good; occasionally flat across the clauses.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-5, exaggerating the rise-then-fall melody.

for_arabic_speakers: A conditional has a MELODY: if-clause rises to the comma ↗, result-clause falls ↘.
'if' is weak and unstressed — the verbs carry the meaning and the stress.
After 'when / as soon as / unless' use the PRESENT tense, not 'will'.
Link 'if I' smoothly (/ɪfaɪ/) and contract the result ('I'll').
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; compare day 7 with day 1.
